scores.claim_text: 1,153 Kohl's stores as of Jan 31 2026; 2 new openings in 2025; 27 underperforming stores closed in 2024; San Bernardino + Monroe e-comm fulfillment centers closed.
scores.M_check: Self-corroboration via EDGAR FTS for exact phrase '1,153 Kohl' returned 0 (EDGAR FTS limitation — phrase parsing). Mall-REIT cross-check: SPG 10-K historically mentioned Kohl's (4 hits 2020-2023) but not in 2024 or 2025 10-K. MAC (Macerich) 10-K never mentions Kohl's. This is consistent with Kohl's being a mostly off-mall big-box anchor at strip centers and power centers rather than enclosed-mall mall-REIT tenant — KSS is largely on its own pad sites and shopping centers held by smaller landlords. Disappearance from SPG's most recent disclosure is mildly notable but is the expected pattern for declining tenant exposure.
scores.M_value: SPG: 4 hits 2020-2023, 0 in 2024-2025. MAC: 0 hits ever. KSS store count 1,153 vs prior reporting cadence consistent.
scores.interpretation: PASS — store count is internally consistent. Net trajectory: 27 closed + 2 opened = net negative footprint. No contradiction; this is a slow-bleed retail footprint reduction. Counterparty absence from mall-REIT tenant rosters is structurally expected for Kohl's (off-mall format).

scores.claim_text: Net sales decreased 4.0% to $14.775B in fiscal 2025; transaction volume down ~4%; all lines of business except Accessories declined.
scores.M_check: Wholesale-supplier counterparty corroboration via EDGAR FTS: Hanesbrands (HBI) mentioned Kohl's in 7 filings, MOST RECENT 2023 10-K — ZERO mentions in 2024 or 2025 10-Ks. Levi (LEVI) only one historical mention (2023). VF Corp (VFC) last mentioned Kohl's in 2019. Calibration Heuristic 7 / Calibration note: while disappearance is consistent with KSS not crossing the 10%-customer-disclosure threshold for these brands, the FADING TIMELINE (HBI: 7 hits 2018-2023, none after) is consistent with a multi-year decline in Kohl's wholesale-importance footprint to apparel brands as Kohl's transformation pivots to private-label + Sephora. This corroborates the disclosed comp-sales decline trajectory.
scores.M_value: HBI: last mention 2023 10-K. LEVI: 1 historical mention. VFC: last mention 2019 10-K. Counterparty wholesale-importance is decaying.
scores.interpretation: MODE — comp-sales decline is honestly disclosed in financial-statement notes (-4.0% revenue, -4% transactions). Counterparty 10-Ks corroborate that Kohl's wholesale-channel importance to top apparel brands has faded over time. The MD&A narrative ('strong inventory management,' 'gross margin +34bps') frames the decline mildly, but the underlying numbers are not hidden. Severity MODE not PASS because the multi-year revenue erosion (transactions -4%, sales -4%, no positive line-of-business growth ex-Accessories) is structural, not cyclical.

scores.claim_text: Moody's downgraded corporate credit Ba3->B2 in 2025; senior unsecured B1->B3. S&P BB- -> B+. 10.000% senior secured notes due 2030 issued in 2025 ($360M). 3.375% notes due 2031 coupon stepped up 175bps cumulative.
scores.M_check: Self-corroboration: '10.000%' phrase appears in 11 filings (10-K, 10-Q x 3, 8-K x 7) including the May 16, 2025 issuance 8-K (accession 0001193125-25-121073), May 30 8-K, multiple follow-on 8-Ks, and the latest 10-K. 8-Ks dated 2025-05-16, 2025-05-30, 2025-08-27, 2025-11-25, 2026-03-10 show ongoing high-yield refinancing activity. External corroboration: 'Kohl' as a bare term appears in 739 10-K/10-Q filings (broad mention universe — typical for a name-brand retailer; not discriminative alone).
scores.M_value: 11 internal filings reference the 10% coupon; ratings disclosure consistent with 5+ refinancing 8-Ks in 2025-2026.
scores.interpretation: SEVE — A 10.000% coupon on senior SECURED paper is a distressed-grade pricing signal. The cumulative 175bps step-up on the 3.375% 2031 notes (coupon adjustment provision tied to ratings) means the company is structurally absorbing higher interest cost for years. Three rating agencies all downgraded; Moody's senior unsecured at B3 is deep in single-B territory. Layer 3 Rule 10: while not a going-concern flag yet, the cluster of distress markers (downgrades, secured-coupon spike, springing covenants, fading wholesale-supplier disclosures) is consistent with the slow-bleed retail distress profile flagged in the cohort calibration note. Pair with tighter-than-default exit window.

scores.claim_text: Kohl's private label and co-branded credit card accounts owned by Capital One (third party); Kohl's shares net risk-adjusted revenue; other revenue -$84M in 2025 partly due to account-servicing shift to Capital One.
scores.M_check: Self-disclosure of 'Capital One' appears 20 times in KSS filings (10-K/10-Q from 2018-2024, plus exhibit 10.13 for the 2022 Amended and Restated Credit Card Program Agreement). Counterparty corroboration: 'Kohl' substring in COF's 10-K/10-Q returns 0 hits. COF discloses partner-bank arrangements broadly but apparently does not name Kohl's individually in its filings — KSS card program is not material to COF at the disclosure threshold.
scores.interpretation: PASS — asymmetric mention pattern is structurally expected (Capital One's domestic card book has thousands of accounts and Kohl's program is well below COF disclosure thresholds). The partnership is well-documented via the public credit-card program agreement exhibit; no contradiction. Severity PASS — no distress signal here, but the $84M YoY decrease in other revenue suggests the credit-card economics are weakening alongside core retail.

scores.claim_text: 1,149 Sephora at Kohl's shop-in-shops (855 full-size + 294 small-format) across 1,100+ stores at year-end 2025. Accessories (incl. Sephora) was the only line of business to grow (+2.0%) in 2025.
scores.M_check: Self-corroboration: 'Sephora' appears in 69 KSS filings. External corroboration (any filer): 'Sephora at Kohl' appears in 37 filings, though most hits are KSS's own 8-Ks since LVMH/Sephora is private and does not file in EDGAR. Sephora Beauty rollout cadence has progressed from initial Dec-2020 8-K announcement through 2024-2026 updates. Calibration Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational): announced 850 full-size shops over time has been EXECUTED (855 reported); the small-format roll-out adds 294 more. Operational execution matches announced cadence.
scores.M_value: 37 external EDGAR mentions of 'Sephora at Kohl'; 69 KSS self-mentions; 1,149 actual shops vs original 850-shop announcement.
scores.interpretation: PASS — Sephora partnership is real, executed, and a verified bright-spot supporting the +2.0% Accessories line. No marketing-vs-operational gap. Note: this also means the rest of the business (-5% to -7% across remaining segments) absent the Sephora halo is performing materially worse than the headline 4% decline.

scores.claim_text: Operating lease ROU $2.338B, operating lease liabilities $2.744B; finance leases + financing obligations $2.450B. Combined ~$5.2B lease/financing liability vs $4.048B shareholders equity at Jan 31 2026.
scores.M_check: Self-corroboration of balance-sheet numbers visible in the 10-K balance sheet table. Counterparty cross-check (mall-REIT side, already run in claim 1): SPG dropped Kohl's from 10-K mentions in 2024-2025; MAC never mentioned Kohl's. This is consistent with Kohl's primary landlord exposure being to smaller, non-public landlords + own-property (Kohl's owns a meaningful fraction of its real estate). Lease-maturity ladder disclosed in notes consistent with a long-tail commitment. Heuristic 12: combined off-debt lease + financing obligations of $5.2B exceeds book equity, a structural risk that headline equity ratios understate.
scores.M_value: Combined lease liability $5.2B vs $4.05B equity. Operating lease ladder long-tail.
scores.interpretation: MODE — the lease/financing-obligation footprint is large relative to equity and constitutes a real fixed-cost overhang. The disclosure itself is complete (balance sheet + notes). Severity MODE because the magnitude is a structural risk; not SEVE because Kohl's owns a meaningful portion of its store fleet (Property and equipment net $6.914B suggests substantial owned real estate) and was able to NEGOTIATE lease terminations favorably in 2024 (the $18M lease gain disclosure).

scores.claim_text: Springing financial covenant on FCCR in $1.5B ABL revolver; in compliance as of Jan 31 2026; zero revolver borrowings outstanding; cash $674M (vs $134M PY).
scores.M_check: Self-corroboration: 'springing' appears in 19 KSS filings — consistent disclosure across 10-K and 10-Q history. 'Going concern' appears in 6 filings, all pre-2024 (most recent: 2023-01-19 8-K which was the credit agreement amendment). No going-concern mention in any post-2023 filing. Layer 3 Rule 10: no form-15, no 25-NSE, no going-concern qualifier in audit report, no covenant waiver disclosed. Cash position improved materially YoY ($134M to $674M).
scores.M_value: springing: 19 hits. going-concern: 6 hits, none after 2023. EY audit report is unqualified.
scores.interpretation: PASS — covenant compliance is real and corroborated; the springing nature of the FCCR test means it doesn't activate unless availability drops below threshold, but availability was high in 2025. The $935M adjusted free cash flow generation (driven by working-capital release via 7% inventory reduction + $129M interchange-litigation settlement) bought the company meaningful runway. Severity PASS — this is the cleanest part of the disclosure. However, $129M of the FCF benefit is non-recurring.

scores.claim_text: Buchanan joined as CEO Jan 15 2025 replacing Kingsbury. 10-K characterizes this as orderly leadership transition.
scores.M_check: Self-corroboration via 8-K filings: 'Buchanan' appears in 8 KSS 8-K filings. CRITICAL FINDING in 2025-05-01 8-K (accession 0001193125-25-109074): 'On April 30, 2025, the Board of Directors of the Company terminated J. Ashley Buchanan as the Company's Chief Executive Officer for Cause (as defined in the Executive Compensation Agreement dated as of January 15, 2025)...' — Buchanan was TERMINATED FOR CAUSE on April 30, 2025, ~3.5 months after joining. The 10-K filed March 19, 2026 (after this event) lists Buchanan's offer letter, ECA, and RSU agreements as exhibits but the prompt-summary 10-K narrative I sliced did not surface 'for cause' termination disclosure. Additional finding: dividend cut from $0.50/qtr to $0.125/qtr (75% reduction) announced March 11, 2025. Activist Macellum Badger relationship goes back to 2021, with formal Cooperation Agreement Feb 2023 (21 hits across KSS filings).
scores.M_value: Buchanan: 8 self-mentions including the for-cause termination 8-K dated May 1, 2025. Macellum: 21 hits. Dividend: cut 75% in March 2025.
scores.interpretation: RED — for-cause CEO termination ~3.5 months into tenure is an extremely high-severity governance event. The pattern (activist 2021 -> Cooperation 2023 -> Kingsbury CEO -> Buchanan CEO Jan 2025 -> for-cause termination April 2025 + 75% dividend cut) is consistent with a deeply unstable governance and strategic-direction situation. Combined with credit downgrades (claim 3), the cluster of distress markers aligns with the cohort's slow-bleed retail distress thesis. Layer 3 Rule 10 elevation: not a delisting/going-concern marker per se, but governance instability of this severity should compound the credit-quality concerns. Falsification window should be tightened from default 12 months.
